title: Cabin in the Sky and Ethel Waters
summary: Greer recalls Ethel Waters from the Cotton Club, and how he handled her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Right. You know what? You probably -- the incidents you remember with Ray Nance probably happened when you all were making "Cabin in the Sky."
Yeah, because Nance wasn't in the band when you all made Murder at the Vanities (Phonetic). He hadn't joined the band yet.

No. Buck and Bubbles was in Cabin in the Sky. Ethel Waters, the hit song from that picture was (humming). She sang -- what was the name of that? "Cabin in the Sky." Yeah, beautiful. She always used it to the day she died. That was one of her main songs. Nobody could sing it like --
What kind of a person was she?
Beautiful. Very -- Ethel Waters was -- I knew her from working with her at the Cotton Club. Because I used to get a little extra taste on the side for talking to

her. She used to sing, 'I'm going to sit down/-- ain't going to give it away, I'm going to sit down on it.' And I used to, She liked it so much she would always put something in my pockets, a little taste in my -- because I wouldn't do nothing, I wouldn't say hello if I didn't get some money.

But me and her was like that. Great. She was going with Eddie Mallory then, you know. Very hard to get along with. She didn't take no back -- took off of nobody. I got along good with her because when she started to get tight with me, I would dummy up on her and not say nothing. In the songs, when she was going to say -- I'd say nothing. It would break her heart. 'Why do you talk to them?' I'd say, 'Well, I didn't figure you was talking to me.' Then we'd go right back, catch up, that money going right on.
She was beautiful. But you had to know how --
: Had to know how to handle her?
